outputs.L1: An active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly for conveying a fluid is disclosed. The assembly comprises a rotor assembly and a bearing assembly configured to support the rotor assembly without contact. The bearing assembly comprises an even number of electromagnetic units arranged around a central structure, each electromagnetic unit comprising a first salient formed of a magnetic material, a permanent magnet providing a first magnetic pole, and a coil arranged around the salient. The bearing assembly further comprises an inner yoke having inner yoke portions connected to the first salient of each electromagnetic unit and separated from one another by structural spacers, thereby providing a closed first magnetic flux passing through the rotor assembly and applying a first attractive force. The bearing assembly further comprises a position-stabilizing portion perpendicular to the first attractive force on the rotor assembly, and the coils provide an electromagnetic flux between each first salient and the rotor assembly for applying an adaptable axial force and/or tilting torque to the rotor assembly.
outputs.L2: Disclosed is an active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly for transporting a fluid. The assembly includes a rotor assembly and a bearing assembly that supports the rotor assembly without physical contact. The bearing assembly has an even number of electromagnetic units positioned around a central structure. Each electromagnetic unit includes a first salient made of magnetic material, a permanent magnet that creates a first magnetic pole, and a coil surrounding the salient. The bearing assembly also includes an inner yoke having yoke portions connected to the first salient of each electromagnetic unit, with the yoke portions separated from one another by structural spacers. This arrangement creates a closed first magnetic flux that passes through the rotor assembly and applies a first attractive force, including a position-stabilizing component acting perpendicular to that first attractive force on the rotor assembly. The coils generate an electromagnetic flux between each first salient and the rotor assembly to apply an adjustable axial force and/or tilting torque to the rotor assembly.
outputs.L3:
An active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly is designed to convey a fluid by means of a rotor assembly. During operation, the rotor assembly is driven to move the fluid through the device, while the bearing assembly supports and stabilizes the rotor assembly without requiring mechanical contact. This contactless support reduces friction, minimizes wear, and can improve the efficiency and service life of the system.

The bearing assembly includes an even number of electromagnetic units arranged circumferentially around a central structure. These electromagnetic units are positioned to interact magnetically with the rotor assembly and to maintain its desired position during operation. The symmetrical arrangement of the electromagnetic units allows controlled magnetic forces to be applied in a balanced and responsive manner.

Each electromagnetic unit includes a magnetic salient, a permanent magnet, and a coil. The permanent magnet provides a baseline magnetic field, while the coil can be selectively energized to modify or supplement that field. The magnetic salient helps guide and concentrate the magnetic flux toward the rotor assembly, improving the effectiveness of the magnetic interaction.

By controlling current supplied to the coils, the electromagnetic units generate electromagnetic flux that applies an adaptable axial force and/or tilting torque to the rotor assembly. This enables active control of the rotor position and orientation, helping to stabilize the rotor assembly during fluid conveyance and compensate for operating disturbances or changing load conditions.
outputs.L4:
An active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly for fluid conveyance is designed to support and control a rotating member without mechanical contact. The assembly includes a rotor and a stator structure arranged around the rotor, with multiple electromagnetic units positioned at substantially equal intervals around the rotational axis. Each electromagnetic unit includes a permanent magnet, an excitation coil, magnetic salients, and inter-yoke portions that cooperate to form controlled magnetic circuits. These components are arranged so that magnetic flux can pass through the stator, across an air gap, into the rotor, and back through the magnetic structure, thereby creating closed magnetic flux paths.

During operation, the permanent magnets provide a bias magnetic field that generates an attractive force between the stator and the rotor. The coils are selectively energized to adjust the magnitude and distribution of the magnetic field in each electromagnetic unit. By controlling the current supplied to the coils, the assembly can actively regulate the radial support forces acting on the rotor, maintaining the rotor in a desired contactless position even while the rotor is spinning and fluid is being conveyed. Because the rotor is suspended magnetically rather than supported by conventional mechanical bearings, friction, wear, lubrication requirements, and particle generation can be reduced.

The salients and inter-yoke portions help guide and concentrate the magnetic flux so that the generated forces act efficiently on the rotor. The symmetrical arrangement of the electromagnetic units allows the system to produce balanced supporting forces under normal operating conditions, while also enabling differential control when correction is needed. If the rotor shifts from its target position, sensors and control circuitry may detect the displacement and adjust coil currents to restore the rotor to the desired alignment.

In addition to radial support, the assembly can produce an adjustable axial force and a controlled tilting torque. By varying the excitation of selected coils, the magnetic field can be made stronger on one side or in one axial region than another, thereby generating forces that correct axial displacement or angular inclination of the rotor. This makes it possible to control not only the position of the rotor in the radial direction, but also its axial location and attitude relative to the stator.

As a result, the active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly provides stable, contactless rotor positioning suitable for pumps, compressors, and other fluid conveyance devices. The use of closed magnetic flux paths improves magnetic efficiency and helps generate strong attractive and stabilizing forces. The ability to actively adjust force and torque allows precise control of rotor motion, enhances operational reliability, and reduces the disadvantages associated with conventional bearing contact.
outputs.L5:
An active magnetic system is a technology that uses controlled magnetic fields to influence, move, or stabilize objects without direct physical contact. Unlike a passive magnet, which has a fixed magnetic force, an active magnetic device can be adjusted in real time. This is usually done with electromagnets, sensors, and control software.

One common example is active magnetic levitation. In this system, magnets lift an object and keep it suspended in the air. Sensors constantly measure the object’s position, while a controller changes the strength of the magnetic field to keep it stable. This technology is used in high-speed maglev trains, precision machinery, and advanced industrial equipment.

Active magnetic systems are also important in medicine and science. Magnetic resonance imaging, known as MRI, uses strong magnetic fields to create detailed images of the human body. In laboratories, active magnetic control can help guide tiny particles, separate materials, or support delicate experiments.

The main advantage of an active magnetic system is precision. Because the magnetic field can be controlled electronically, it can respond quickly to changes. This reduces friction, improves efficiency, and allows movement without mechanical wear. As technology develops, active magnetic systems are expected to play an even greater role in transportation, healthcare, robotics, and clean energy solutions.

counterfactuals.output:
1. A contactless active magnetic bearing for supporting a pump rotor, comprising:  

an annular central structure configured to surround or be surrounded by the pump rotor and to define a rotor-receiving axis;  

an even number of electromagnetic units disposed circumferentially about the central structure in opposed pairs, each electromagnetic unit comprising:  

a salient pole portion facing the pump rotor across an air gap;  

a permanent magnet arranged to provide a bias magnetic flux through the salient pole portion; and

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a dense patent-like summary for an invention involving an active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly for conveying a fluid, emphasizing closed magnetic flux through the rotor assembly and controllable axial force or tilting torque from coils.
counterfactuals.output:
An active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly for conveying a fluid comprises a rotor assembly disposed in a flow passage and configured to impart energy to the fluid, the rotor assembly including an impeller, hub, or pump rotor coupled to a ferromagnetic or permanent-magnet magnetic circuit portion, and a stator assembly arranged radially and/or axially outwardly of the rotor assembly and separated therefrom by one or more fluid gaps. The rotor assembly is configured such that a substantial portion of magnetic flux generated by rotor magnets and/or stator excitation elements closes through the rotor assembly itself, including through circumferentially or axially spaced rotor flux-return portions, thereby reducing stray flux, increasing force density, and enabling compact integration of magnetic suspension and fluid-conveying functions.

The stator assembly includes a plurality of independently controllable electromagnetic coils disposed about the rotor assembly and magnetically coupled to pole pieces or yoke portions positioned to interact with corresponding rotor magnetic portions. Selective energization of the coils produces controlled magnetic attraction and/or reluctance forces across the fluid gaps to generate an axial force for positioning, unloading, or biasing the rotor assembly along a rotational axis. Differential energization of opposed or angularly spaced coils produces a controllable tilting torque about one or more transverse axes, thereby actively regulating rotor attitude, suppressing vibration, compensating hydraulic thrust, and maintaining clearance between rotating and stationary components during operation.

In one implementation, the rotor assembly includes axially spaced magnetic pole regions joined by a rotor back-iron or flux bridge so that magnetic flux passes from a stator pole across a first air or fluid gap into the rotor, through the rotor flux-return path, and back across a second gap to a stator return pole, forming a substantially closed magnetic circuit through the rotor assembly. In another implementation, permanent magnets carried by the rotor are oriented to establish a closed internal flux path, while stator coils superimpose controllable flux components for axial centering and tilt control. The coils may be driven by a controller responsive to position, current, pressure, flow, speed, or vibration signals to provide closed-loop magnetic bearing control simultaneously with operation of the rotor as a pump, compressor, blower, turbine, or other fluid mover.

The assembly may be configured as a bearingless motor, an active thrust bearing, an active radial/tilt bearing, or a combined hydrodynamic and magnetic support system. The fluid being conveyed may occupy the magnetic gap and may provide cooling and lubrication-free operation, while the magnetic bearing forces maintain non-contact support of the rotor. By directing magnetic flux through closed paths in the rotor assembly and by using controllable coil excitation to generate axial force and tilting torque, the invention provides a compact, sealed, low-wear fluid-conveying rotor system with improved stability, controllability, efficiency, and reduced contamination risk relative to mechanically supported rotor assemblies.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following concept into patent language: a rotor for fluid transport is supported without contact by electromagnetic units arranged around it, where each unit has a magnetic salient, permanent magnet, coil, and yoke portions separated by structural spacers to provide stabilizing magnetic forces.
counterfactuals.output:
A contactless fluid-transport apparatus comprising a rotor configured to impart motion to a fluid and a plurality of electromagnetic support units disposed circumferentially about the rotor, the electromagnetic support units being configured to support the rotor in a non-contact state during operation.

Each electromagnetic support unit comprises a magnetic salient portion facing the rotor, at least one permanent magnet, at least one electromagnetic coil, and a plurality of yoke portions forming part of a magnetic flux path. The yoke portions are spaced apart by structural spacer members, the spacer members maintaining a predetermined relative position between the yoke portions and defining magnetic gaps within the electromagnetic support unit.

The permanent magnet and the coil are arranged with the magnetic salient portion and the yoke portions such that magnetic flux generated by the permanent magnet and controllable magnetic flux generated by the coil are directed through the magnetic salient portion toward the rotor. The electromagnetic support units are thereby operable to generate stabilizing magnetic forces acting on the rotor to maintain the rotor in a desired radial and/or axial position without mechanical contact while the rotor transports fluid.
